correction.text: the Bishopric of Ösel-Wiek: Saare, Hiiu and Lääne counties and the western part of Pärnu county, as the page names them

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no row for the Bishopric of Ösel-Wiek (its Livonian Conference row of 1422-1561 covers Old Livonia as a whole). The page says the bishopric covered 'what are now Saare, Hiiu, Lääne counties and the western part of Pärnu county', with Ösel (Saaremaa) and Dagö (Hiiumaa) named; no boundary. The western part of Pärnu county is drawn as the part west of 24.4 E (the researcher's cut).

region.text: the Bishopric of Ösel-Wiek: Saare, Hiiu and Lääne counties and the western part of Pärnu county, as the page names them

ledger.note: 1 October 1228: the bishopric is created. 'The bishopric was created on 1 October 1228 as a Latin rite' diocese, covering Saare, Hiiu, Lääne and western Pärnu counties; successively known as bishopric of Leal (Lihula) from 1234. The page does not describe the conquest of Saaremaa (1227, in the ancient-estonia dossier), so the previous holder is carried as the Brothers of the Sword who took the island.
1251: the seat moves to Perona (Vana-Pärnu): 'Perona (Vana-Pärnu) from 1251'.
1279: the seat moves to Hapsal (Haapsalu) Castle: 'Hapsal (Haapsalu) Castle from 1279'.

region.text: the Bishopric of Ösel-Wiek: Saare, Hiiu and Lääne counties and the western part of Pärnu county, as the page names them

ledger.note: 26 September 1559: the bishop signs away the territory. 'Bishop Johann von Münchhausen signed a treaty on 26 September 1559' giving Frederick II of Denmark the right to nominate the bishop, 'an act which amounted to the sale of these territories for 30,000 thalers'. The Livonian Conference dossier files the same treaty as a loss to denmark-norway.

region.text: the Bishopric of Ösel-Wiek: Saare, Hiiu and Lääne counties and the western part of Pärnu county, as the page names them

ledger.note: April 1560: Magnus takes possession, 'who then took possession in April 1560'. The Ösel-Wiek page: Magnus obtained it as an appanage on 15 April 1560.

region.text: the Bishopric of Ösel-Wiek: Saare, Hiiu and Lääne counties and the western part of Pärnu county, as the page names them

ledger.note: April 1560: the territory passes to Denmark. 'The principality ceased to exist in 1560'; the last prince-bishop, Johannes V von Münchhausen, sold it to Denmark, and Magnus of Livonia 'obtained it as an appanage on 15 April 1560'. The page's bishop list shows Magnus serving 1560-1572 but gives no 1572 end for the principality.

certainty.note: The page names the four counties only; the Estonian county borders stand for the bishopric's boundary. The Ösel autonomy of 1241-1343 (renewed 27 August 1255) is internal and not drawn.

sources.title: Livonian War
sources.note: 26 September 1559 treaty with Frederick II, Magnus took possession in April 1560.

notes: Ecclesiastical principality of Terra Mariana. The Ösel-Wiek page gives the end as 1560 (sold to Denmark, Magnus's appanage on 15 April 1560), the Livonian War page gives the 26 September 1559 treaty as the transfer of the right to nominate; the Livonian Conference dossier carries the loss at 1559-9, this dossier carries the treaty as a vassalage (the Danish crown nominating the bishop) and the loss at April 1560 when Magnus took possession. Seat: Leal (Lihula) from 1234 and the Arensburg shift are not drawn (Lihula is not in the gazetteer; the Arensburg year is undated). The page says Denmark ceded Wiek to the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth in exchange for parts of Ösel belonging to the Livonian Order, without a year; the Danish Wiek and Ösel (1560-1645) would need their own dossier (Denmark-Norway files these events under swedish-empire in its own dossier). Review eu-14-x (2026-10-31): capital Leal (Lihula) 1228-1250 added from the infobox.
